Andre Drummond is an American professional basketball player.
Andre Drummond plays for the Philadelphia 76ers in the National Basketball Association (NBA).
Andre Drummond was selected by the Detroit Pistons in the first round of the 2012 NBA draft with the ninth overall pick.
Drummond was one of the top-rated basketball players in the high school class of 2011.
Drummond played one season of college basketball with the Connecticut Huskies before declaring for the draft.
Drummond was named to the NBA All-Rookie Second Team with Detroit in 2013.
Drummond was named an All-Star for the first time in 2016.
Drummond was traded to the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2020.
Drummond reached a buyout agreement with Cleveland in 2021.
Drummond joined the Los Angeles Lakers for the remainder of the 2020–21 season after reaching a buyout agreement with Cleveland.
Drummond has played for the Brooklyn Nets and Chicago Bulls.
Drummond is known as one of the league leaders in rebounding.
Drummond was a member of the 2014 U.S. national team that won a gold medal in the FIBA Basketball World Cup.
Drummond was born on August 10, 1993, in Mount Vernon, New York.
Drummond's parents are Jamaican.
Drummond moved to Middletown, Connecticut with his mother and sister when he was seven years old.
Drummond attended Woodrow Wilson Middle School before starting high school at Capital Preparatory Magnet School in Hartford.
During his freshman year at Capital Preparatory Magnet School, Drummond averaged 12.7 points, 11.9 rebounds, and 6.5 blocks per game.
During his sophomore year at Capital Preparatory Magnet School, Drummond improved to averaging 20.2 points, 16.6 rebounds, 7.2 blocks, and 4.5 steals per game.
Drummond transferred to St. Thomas More in Oakdale after two years at Capital Preparatory Magnet School due to a stress fracture in his foot.
At St. Thomas More, Drummond was one of the most dominating centers in high school basketball.
Drummond led the team to the national prep championship in 2011 during his time at St. Thomas More.
Drummond graduated from St. Thomas More in the spring of 2011.
Drummond was rated as the No. 1 player in the class of 2011 by ESPN and NBADraft.net.
Drummond was ranked No. 2 player by Rivals.com and Scout.com in the class of 2011.
Drummond was a member of the gold medal-winning United States team at the 2010 FIBA Under-17 World Championship.
Drummond initially declared he would spend a postgraduate year at Wilbraham & Monson Academy in 2011–12.
Two weeks later, Drummond announced via Twitter that instead he intended to reclassify and attend the University of Connecticut.
Drummond appeared in 34 games as a freshman at UConn, starting 30 times.
Drummond averaged 28.4 minutes per game during his freshman season with UConn.
During his freshman year at UConn, Drummond scored an average of 10.0 points and grabbed 7.6 rebounds per game.
Drummond led the team in rebounds per game as a freshman.
Drummond had 2.7 blocks per game on average during his freshman season with UConn.
